subject: science
title: States of matter and the water cycle

cards.back: Keeps its own shape and has a fixed volume. Example: ice.
cards.say: solid. Keeps its own shape and has a fixed volume. Example: ice.

cards.back: Flows and takes the shape of its container, but has a fixed volume. Example: water.
cards.say: liquid. Flows and takes the shape of its container, but has a fixed volume. Example: water.

cards.back: Spreads out to fill its container and can be squashed. Example: water vapour.
cards.say: gas. Spreads out to fill its container and can be squashed. Example: water vapour.

cards.back: A solid changing to a liquid when it is heated.
cards.say: melting. A solid changing to a liquid when it is heated.

cards.back: A liquid changing to a solid when it is cooled.
cards.say: freezing. A liquid changing to a solid when it is cooled.

cards.back: A liquid changing to a gas at its surface.
cards.say: evaporation. A liquid changing to a gas at its surface.

cards.back: A liquid changing to a gas throughout the liquid, with bubbles. It happens at the boiling point.
cards.say: boiling. A liquid changing to a gas throughout the liquid, with bubbles. It happens at the boiling point.

cards.back: A gas changing to a liquid when it is cooled.
cards.say: condensation. A gas changing to a liquid when it is cooled.

cards.front: At what temperature does pure water freeze?
cards.back: Zero degrees Celsius.
cards.say: At what temperature does pure water freeze? Zero degrees Celsius.

cards.front: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?
cards.back: One hundred degrees Celsius.
cards.say: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level? One hundred degrees Celsius.

cards.back: Water as an invisible gas in the air.
cards.say: water vapour. Water as an invisible gas in the air.

cards.back: The way water moves around Earth, from the sea to the air to the land and back again.
cards.say: water cycle. The way water moves around Earth, from the sea to the air to the land and back again.

cards.front: What gives the energy that drives the water cycle?
cards.back: The heat of the Sun.
cards.say: What gives the energy that drives the water cycle? The heat of the Sun.

cards.front: Where does water evaporate from in nature?
cards.back: Seas, lakes, rivers, puddles and wet ground. Plants also lose water vapour from their leaves.
cards.say: Where does water evaporate from in nature? Seas, lakes, rivers, puddles and wet ground. Plants also lose water vapour from their leaves.

cards.back: Water vapour rises and cools. It condenses into tiny droplets of liquid water, and many droplets make a cloud.
cards.say: How do clouds form? Water vapour rises and cools. It condenses into tiny droplets of liquid water, and many droplets make a cloud.

cards.back: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
cards.say: precipitation. Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail.

cards.back: Rainwater that flows over the land into streams, rivers and the sea.
cards.say: run-off. Rainwater that flows over the land into streams, rivers and the sea.

cards.front: Where is most of Earth's water found?
cards.back: In the oceans.
cards.say: Where is most of Earth's water found? In the oceans.

cards.front: Why do puddles slowly disappear on a sunny day?
cards.back: The water evaporates and becomes water vapour in the air.
cards.say: Why do puddles slowly disappear on a sunny day? The water evaporates and becomes water vapour in the air.

cards.front: Why do drops of water form outside a cold glass?
cards.back: Water vapour in the air touches the cold glass and condenses into liquid.
cards.say: Why do drops of water form outside a cold glass? Water vapour in the air touches the cold glass and condenses into liquid.

cards.front: What happens to particles when ice is heated?
cards.back: They vibrate more and more until they break free of their fixed places, and the ice melts.
cards.say: What happens to particles when ice is heated? They vibrate more and more until they break free of their fixed places, and the ice melts.

cards.front: When ice melts, does its mass change?
cards.back: No. The mass stays the same, because the same amount of matter is there.
cards.say: When ice melts, does its mass change? No. The mass stays the same, because the same amount of matter is there.

cards.front: Does melting take in heat or give out heat?
cards.back: It takes in heat. Freezing is the opposite and gives out heat.
cards.say: Does melting take in heat or give out heat? It takes in heat. Freezing is the opposite and gives out heat.
